items.description: The default `env_scrub` list (design D5, nightly-config.schema.json `env_scrub.default`) misses credential variables the skills' coordination bridge actually reads. `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/coordination_bridge.py` resolves the API key from `_API_KEY_ENV_KEYS = (COORDINATION_API_KEY, COORDINATOR_API_KEY)` and Cloudflare Access service tokens from `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` / `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET`; URL aliases `COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL`, `AGENT_COORDINATOR_API_URL`, `AGENT_COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL` and `AGENT_COORDINATOR_REST_PORT` are also unscrubbed. The `COORDINATION_API_URL` sentinel wins URL precedence today, but `COORDINATOR_API_KEY` and the CF tokens still reach every fixture agent, and any future reordering or a non-loopback sentinel (rejected by `_validate_url`, falls through to `http://localhost:3000`) re-opens the live-coordinator path. The `always_scrub` set only covers `gaps.api_key_env`.
items.resolution: adjudicated valid (verified coordination_bridge.py _HTTP_URL_ENV_KEYS/_API_KEY_ENV_KEYS/CF_ACCESS_*): built-in HERMETIC_SCRUB denylist covers all bridge URL/key/CF vars + drift test (D5, spec, task 1.2)

items.description: D3 asserts that `/improve-harness` dedup collapses multi-vendor failures of one gate in one run into a single occurrence so frequency counts nights. That is not what the consumer does: in `skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py` `main()` computes `deduplicate_findings(...)` and discards it (an in-source `BUG:` note says so), then calls `rank_findings(memory_entries)`, whose `frequency` is `len(gap_entries)` over raw memory entries. With two vendors failing the same gate, one night contributes frequency 2, not 1. Task 4.4's 'frequency 2 from two runs' assertion passes, but for a different reason than the design states, and the plan's trend reasoning ('frequency rises night over night') is off by the vendor count.
items.resolution: fixed with #16

items.description: Group 4 check: the requirement 'Skill under test is materialized from the checkout being evaluated' contains the clause 'SHALL record the skills revision on each result', but none of its three scenarios (skill copied, missing skill, timeout) has a WHEN/THEN asserting `skills_sha` (or `+dirty`) on a result record; the 'results are appended' scenario's required-field list also omits it. Likewise the 'Durable per-vendor per-skill results store' requirement promises filtering by 'skill family, scenario and time window' but only vendor, skill and `--since` are scenario-covered. Task 1.4 tests `skills_sha` and task 3.3 tests filters, so implementation intent exists; the spec just does not pin it.
items.resolution: fixed: skills_sha asserted in materialization scenario and result field list; family/scenario/--until query scenario added

items.description: The nightly-config schema lists `enabled` and `caps` as `required` (and `caps` requires all four sub-keys) while also declaring `default` values for them, and proposal.md's NFR table and design D4 describe `max_pairs` 30 / `max_pairs_per_vendor` 15 / `max_wall_clock_minutes` 240 / `per_pair_timeout_seconds` 1200 as defaults. A config that relies on the documented defaults fails guard 0 (exit 2). Separately, D4 shows `disable_file: ~/.config/agent-scenarios/DISABLED` as the default kill-file but the schema gives `disable_file` no default, so the design's 'kill-file' off-switch does not exist unless the operator spells it out.
items.resolution: fixed: enabled/caps no longer required, caps sub-keys optional with defaults, disable_file default ~/.config/agent-scenarios/DISABLED

items.description: Design D3 bounds each `failed_gates[].detail` to 500 characters so command-gate output cannot bloat memory, but the capability-gap-entry contract does not encode it; only task 4.1's unit test does. The contract is what the skills-side consumer test validates against, so a future emitter that drops the truncation would still pass the schema.
items.resolution: fixed: detail maxLength 500

items.description: Hermeticity rests on an operator-editable `env_set` with no validation: the schema accepts any string map, and the spec scenario pins `COORDINATION_API_URL` only to 'the configured env_set value'. A config with `env_set: {}` or `env_set: {COORDINATION_API_URL: https://coord.rotkohl.ai}` passes guard 0 and fixture agents take locks and write memories in production, which is exactly the failure plan-finding #3 was meant to close.
items.resolution: fixed with #14

items.description: Token scrubbing plus the `gh` shim covers the GitHub API path, but not git transport: an agent can still `git push` to a real GitHub remote via SSH keys, a credential helper, or `insteadOf` rewrites in the nightly user's `~/.gitconfig`/`~/.ssh`. The design delegates this to the operator (dedicated HOME, task 7.1), so it is not test-verifiable.
items.resolution: fixed: git transport credentials named in D5 + residual risk; task 7.1 requires a HOME without GitHub push credentials

items.description: ri-15's change `build-agent-trajectory-scenario-harness` is merged in code but not archived: it still lives under `openspec/changes/` and there is no `openspec/specs/agent-trajectory-harness/spec.md`. This change's `agent-trajectory-harness` delta is therefore ADDED-only against a capability that does not yet exist in `openspec/specs/`, which is valid, and the revised `implement-feature-basic` still satisfies ri-15's 'Seed scenarios exercising plan and implement skills' requirement (verify + prohibit gates, two vendors). But archive order matters: archiving ri-16 before ri-15 would create the capability spec from ri-16's deltas alone, and ri-15's later archive must then merge into it.
items.resolution: fixed: archive-order note in proposal Impact + task 6.4

items.description: The `run` record schema carries `repo_sha`, `skills_sha` and `reason` that design D2's `run` field list (`run_id, started_at, finished_at, status, planned_pairs, executed_pairs, config_digest, vendors`) does not mention, and `finished_at` is optional in the schema although D2 lists it as a run field. Minor drift between the design and the contract that the record-shape tests (3.1) will pin one way or the other.
items.resolution: fixed: D2 run field list includes repo_sha/skills_sha/reason; finished_at required

items.description: Because the `run` record is written last, 'no run record for this run_id' is also the state of the currently executing nightly. A `results query`/`latest` run during the 02:30–06:30 window labels the live run as interrupted, which will mislead the runbook triage step and any future dispatcher gate reading `latest`.
items.resolution: fixed: lock-held runs reported as in progress (D2, spec scenario, task 3.1)

items.description: Critical: The plan fixes skill availability but not skill invocation. `design.md` D5 only copies the skills tree, while `CLIVendorExecutor` still gives the vendor a natural-language task prompt with no requirement or gate proving that `skill_under_test` was loaded or followed. Task 6.1 uses a custom fake executor that deliberately reads the break marker, so it can pass even if live vendors bypass the skill entirely. Define a vendor-neutral invocation/verification mechanism and test it through the real CLI-adapter path.
items.resolution: adjudicated partially valid: seed task_prompts must invoke /<skill_under_test>, guard-tested (D5/D6, spec coverage-floor scenario, tasks 2.1/2.4/2.5); skill-following verified via skill-distinctive gates and recorded as residual risk. Rejected: testing through the real CLI adapter (no paid vendor runs in tests; live drill is task 7.5)

items.description: Critical: `design.md` lines 162-166 incorrectly state that `/improve-harness` needs no code change. Its current query is incompatible with `POST /memory/query`: it sends no API key or required `agent_id`, sends unsupported `time_window_days`, and reads `entries` although the API returns a `memories` envelope. Task 4.4 bypasses this path by feeding fixtures directly into normalization/ranking, so the planned tests would pass while emitted gaps remain invisible. Add the consumer/API changes and an authenticated store-then-query integration test.
items.resolution: adjudicated valid (verified MemoryQueryRequest requires agent_id, verify_api_key, list_envelope('memories'); analyze_failures sends none and reads 'entries'): D3 corrected, task 4.4a repairs query_memory, 4.4 tests against an API-shaped stub, harness-engineering scenario added, wp-gaps scope extended

items.description: Critical: `wp-nightly` is specified to wire results through `suite.skill_family`, but `suite.py` is created by `wp-scenarios` and `wp-nightly` depends only on foundation, results, and gaps (`work-packages.yaml` lines 400-403). In isolated worktrees the nightly package can therefore start without the module it must import. Add `wp-scenarios` as a dependency of `wp-nightly`, or move the shared family mapping into a prerequisite package.
items.resolution: adjudicated valid: wp-nightly now depends on wp-scenarios (suite.skill_family)

items.description: Critical: The absolute requirement that live runs never reach the real coordinator is not enforced fail-closed. A schema-valid config can replace `env_scrub` or set `env_set` to an empty/live value, and D5 explicitly leaves user-HOME MCP coordinator access to a post-merge operator task. Such a run can execute fixture agents with a live coordinator transport despite the stated hermeticity guarantee. Make the coordinator/GitHub denylist and unreachable coordinator override non-overridable safety controls, and launch vendors with an isolated HOME/XDG/MCP configuration.
items.resolution: adjudicated valid except isolated HOME: denylist non-removable, COORDINATION_API_URL always forced, env_set may not name denylisted vars (schema propertyNames + guard 0), spec scenario 'config cannot re-open the live coordinator path'. Isolated HOME rejected (vendor CLIs auth from HOME); handled by task 7.1 + named residual risk

items.description: Critical: D4 returns exit 0 for `budget_exhausted` when executed pairs passed, while the systemd template treats only exit 0 as success. An incomplete nightly matrix will therefore appear green and trigger no failure handling, even though an arbitrary deterministic tail was never tested. Give incomplete coverage a distinct non-zero exit or configure an explicit notification/health gate for `budget_exhausted`.
items.resolution: adjudicated valid: budget_exhausted without fail exits 3 (D4, spec wall-clock + infra scenarios, task 5.2, proposal NFR)

items.description: Critical: D3's claim that capability-gap frequency counts nights rather than vendors is false for the existing consumer. `analyze_failures.main()` explicitly discards its deduplicated `all_findings` and ranks raw memory entries, and `/memory/query` does not return `session_id`; two vendors failing the same gate in one run therefore count twice. Include `run_id` in returned data (for example in `details`), repair the consumed ranking path, and test two vendors in one run plus a later run.
items.resolution: adjudicated partially valid (verified rank_findings counts raw entries; /memory/query omits session_id): D3 claim corrected to frequency unit (run, vendor), run_id added to details/contract, consumer test pins 2-vendors+later-run=3, new he scenario. Rejected: repairing the consumer ranking path here (the in-source BUG note scopes it to its own change)

items.description: Nit: `results-record.schema.json` is weaker than D2's declared record contract. Result records may omit `trajectory_status`, `duration_seconds`, `repo_sha`, `skills_sha`, and `error`; run records may omit `finished_at`, `vendors`, and `config_digest`; and the schema accepts contradictory states such as `fail` with no failed gates or `error` without an error. Require the declared nullable fields and add status-dependent constraints so consumers can trust schema-valid records.
items.resolution: fixed: nullable D2 fields required; status-dependent if/then constraints

items.description: Nit: The sink plan treats transport reachability as delivery but does not require checking the memory endpoint's application-level response. `POST /memory/store` can return HTTP 200 with `success: false`; if that is treated as delivered, the entry will be removed rather than spooled, violating the zero-loss requirement. Specify that only a valid response with `success: true` acknowledges delivery and add a 200/false replay test.
items.resolution: fixed: only 2xx + success:true acknowledges delivery (D3, spec scenario, task 4.2)

items.description: The ADDED requirement extends the `source` vocabulary, but the base `openspec/specs/harness-engineering/spec.md` requirement 'Capability Gap Detection' still states `source (enum: self-reported, coordinator-emitted, session-log, transcript-mined)` in 'Structured failure recording schema' and 'one or more of: self-reported, coordinator-emitted, session-log, transcript-mined' in 'Report includes source attribution'. The in-flight `add-a-judged-first-stage-to-coordinator-audit-triage` MODIFIED copy keeps both closed lists verbatim (its spec.md lines 9 and 47). After archive the capability spec will contain two requirements that contradict each other on the enum. The decision to ADD rather than MODIFY is sound (delta collision), but the ADDED requirement should say explicitly that it extends the `source` enum of 'Capability Gap Detection' and the two scenarios' source lists, and tasks.md should carry a follow-up note to fold the value into that requirement once the judged-triage change archives.
items.resolution: fixed: ADDED requirement states it extends the Capability Gap Detection enum; D3 base-spec enum note; task 6.4 reconciles at archive

items.description: Group 5 mirrored-copy check: the `env_set.propertyNames.not.enum` list is a second, hand-maintained copy of the executor's `HERMETIC_SCRUB` denylist (plus `COORDINATION_API_URL`). The planned drift test (D5, task 1.2) only asserts `HERMETIC_SCRUB` ⊇ the coordination-bridge variable names; nothing asserts the schema's enum equals `HERMETIC_SCRUB ∪ {COORDINATION_API_URL}`. A later change that adds a name to the Python constant (e.g. a new bridge alias caught by the drift test) leaves the JSON schema, and therefore the promoted package copy and the pydantic `propertyNames` mirror, accepting that name in `env_set`, silently re-opening the path the fail-closed design is meant to shut. Today the 14 names match the design list, so this is a drift risk, not a current defect.
items.resolution: fixed: drift test schema env_set.propertyNames == HERMETIC_SCRUB ∪ {COORDINATION_API_URL} (D5, task 1.2)

items.description: D5 orders the executor as scrub → apply `env_set` → force the sentinel, and the rejection rule for `env_set` keys covers only the built-in denylist and `COORDINATION_API_URL`. Variables that are scrubbed dynamically — names listed in `env_scrub` and the names configured via `gaps.api_key_env` / `gaps.coordinator_url_env` when they are not the defaults — are not rejected, so a config with `gaps.api_key_env: MY_COORD_KEY` and `env_set: {MY_COORD_KEY: ...}` passes guard 0 and re-injects the runner's coordinator credential after the scrub. The spec scenario 'the runner's coordinator credential never reaches an agent' only covers `env_scrub` omitting the name, not `env_set` re-adding it. Low because the default names are in the static enum; the pydantic model (which can see cross-field values) should close it.
items.resolution: fixed: env_set may not name any effective-scrub variable incl. env_scrub entries and gaps.*_env names (D5, spec, task 5.1)

items.description: D5 attributes `COORDINATOR_URL` to the coordination bridge's URL aliases, but `coordination_bridge.py` `_HTTP_URL_ENV_KEYS` is `(COORDINATION_API_URL, COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL, AGENT_COORDINATOR_API_URL, AGENT_COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL)`; `COORDINATOR_URL` is read by `skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py` (and D3 itself says so). Scrubbing it is still right (an improve-harness invocation inside a fixture would otherwise find the live coordinator), but the sentence misattributes the source and the drift test as described would not cover it. Clarify so a future reader does not drop it when reconciling against the bridge.
items.resolution: fixed: COORDINATOR_URL attributed to analyze_failures.py, not the bridge

items.description: wp-integration (tier A, the final gate) runs `skills/tests/improve-harness` and `skills/session-log/tests` but omits `skills/improve-harness/tests`, which task 4.4a explicitly edits (`test_improve_harness.py` pins the old `build_memory_query` payload and must be updated). wp-gaps' own verification does include that directory, so the gap only matters if a later package or the convergence step regresses the skill; but the tier-A gate should cover every touched test tree. Task 6.3 ('skills gate set') is vaguer than the package verification step.
items.resolution: fixed: wp-integration gate runs skills/improve-harness/tests

items.description: Both the new gap sink (D3) and the repaired `analyze_failures.query_memory` (task 4.4a, he spec scenario) authenticate with `X-API-Key`. `coordination_api.verify_api_key` documents that header as 'legacy header retained for backward compatibility' and lists `Authorization: Bearer <key>` as the preferred form. It works today and existing skills use it, so no change is required; noting so the implementer can choose `Authorization: Bearer` (or accept both in the stub test) rather than extending the legacy surface.
items.resolution: fixed (verified verify_api_key: Authorization Bearer preferred, X-API-Key legacy): sink and repaired query use Authorization: Bearer

items.description: Re-verification of open ledger item [8]: still accurate. `openspec/changes/build-agent-trajectory-scenario-harness/` is present and unarchived and `openspec/specs/` has no `agent-trajectory-harness` directory, so this change's ADDED-only delta targets a capability that exists only in ri-15's unarchived delta. None of the requirement names in this delta collide with ri-15's six (`Agent scenario model…`, `Deterministic goal-gate scoring…`, `Injectable per-vendor executor…`, `Injectable additive LLM-judge…`, `Findings emitter…`, `Seed scenarios exercising plan and implement skills`), so either archive order produces a valid merged spec; the only consequence is that ri-15's later archive must merge into a spec created by ri-16. Nothing in tasks.md records the preferred order. Accept as a low operator note.
items.resolution: fixed with #8

items.description: Optional: `specs/harness-engineering/spec.md` adds `scenario-parity` as a source, but the base `Capability Gap Detection` requirement and its in-flight MODIFIED copy still define a closed four-value source enum. Archiving both changes would leave contradictory requirements unless the existing requirement is explicitly extended or a follow-up modification is recorded.
items.resolution: fixed with #19 (codex duplicate)

items.description: Optional: `contracts/schemas/nightly-config.schema.json` independently duplicates the executor's `HERMETIC_SCRUB` names in `env_set.propertyNames`, while the planned drift test checks only the Python denylist against coordination-bridge variables. A later denylist addition could therefore remain schema-accepted and reopen a scrubbed variable through `env_set`. Add a parity assertion between the schema enum and `HERMETIC_SCRUB` plus `COORDINATION_API_URL`.
items.resolution: fixed with #20 (codex duplicate)

items.description: Nit: The static `env_set` prohibition does not cover dynamically configured `gaps.api_key_env`, `gaps.coordinator_url_env`, or additional `env_scrub` names. Because overrides are applied after scrubbing, a valid config can scrub a custom coordinator credential and then re-inject it through `env_set`. Require the Pydantic cross-field validator to reject all dynamically scrubbed names and add a scenario covering reinjection.
items.resolution: fixed with #21 (codex duplicate)

items.description: Nit: `design.md` attributes `COORDINATOR_URL` to `coordination_bridge.py`, but that module's URL aliases do not include it; the variable is read by `skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py`. Scrubbing it is correct, but the attribution and described bridge-only drift test are incomplete and could cause the variable to be dropped during future reconciliation.
items.resolution: fixed with #22 (codex duplicate)

items.description: Nit: The final tier-A `wp-integration` verification runs `skills/tests/improve-harness` and `skills/session-log/tests` but omits `skills/improve-harness/tests`, even though task 4.4a modifies that test tree. The package-specific gate covers it earlier, but the final convergence gate would not catch a later-package regression. Include every touched improve-harness test directory in the final command.
items.resolution: fixed with #23 (codex duplicate)

items.description: run_states() applies one global lock probe to every run id lacking a RunRecord, so while any nightly holds nightly.lock, every older interrupted run (killed before its RunRecord was written) is reported as in_progress instead of interrupted. Only the newest run without a RunRecord can be the live one; older ones are interrupted regardless of the lock. The results CLI and the runbook's 'interrupted vs in_progress' distinction therefore give wrong answers exactly during the window an operator is most likely to query (a run in flight). Suggested fix: when held, label only the most recent unfinished run id (by first-seen order or recorded_at) as in_progress and the rest interrupted.

merge_pr clones the bare origin into a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp directory and never removes it, on either the success or the failure path. Each `gh pr merge` the agent under test issues leaks a full clone under /tmp; a nightly suite running merge-pull-requests scenarios across several vendors leaks one per pair per night, and the nightly's own `_remove_workspace` cannot reclaim them because they live outside the workdir. Wrap the clone in try/finally with shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True), or place the clone under bin_dir_for(workdir) so existing workspace cleanup covers it.

The RunRecord written by finish() stores the configured vendor list, not the effective one. When a vendor is excluded by preflight (CLI unavailable, or the broken-vendor exclusion path that still leaves >=2 effective vendors), the run record claims vendors that never executed, so `results latest`/trend consumers and the runbook's 'which vendors ran' question read a misleading answer. Record the effective vendors (and optionally the excluded ones with a reason) so the ledger reflects what actually ran.

Re-verified ledger [34]: CLIVendorExecutor always calls install_gh_shim(..., origin_path_for(workdir)) even when fixture.local_remote is false. State points origin at a bare repo that was never created; gh pr create/merge then fail inside the shim with opaque git errors and do not append gh-unsupported.log, so the pair becomes a vendor error instead of the designed gh shim: unsupported call message.

The task-4.4a repair added `--agent-id`, `IMPROVE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID`, and `COORDINATION_API_KEY` (Bearer auth) to analyze_failures.py, and the live coordinator at COORDINATOR_URL now rejects unauthenticated /memory/query with 401 (which query_memory reports only as 'Coordinator unreachable' and returns []). SKILL.md's Prerequisites and Step 1 example still describe only COORDINATOR_URL and do not mention the key or agent id, so a user following the skill against a secured coordinator silently gets an empty ranking with a misleading 'unreachable' warning. Document COORDINATION_API_KEY / IMPROVE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID (and the `--agent-id` flag) in Prerequisites, and consider distinguishing HTTP 401/403 from a connection failure in the warning text.

The broken-skill acceptance test only exercises the improve-harness ranking assertion when skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py exists on disk; otherwise it silently passes without checking that the emitted capability-gap entries rank the broken skill first. Because this file lives at a fixed repo-relative path and the test is the acceptance evidence for design D3/D4 ('improve-harness surfaces the gap'), a rename or a packaging layout where the skills tree is absent turns the key assertion into a no-op green. Use pytest.skip with a reason (visible in the summary) or make the path a hard assertion so the gap is reported rather than hidden.

The shim's shebang interpolates sys.executable verbatim. Linux shebangs do not support spaces or quoting, so a venv under a path containing a space (common on dev laptops with `~/My Projects/...`) yields a shim that cannot be executed and every `gh` call fails with ENOENT-style errors rather than the designed unsupported-call path. Low likelihood in the nightly deployment (systemd unit, fixed path); if it matters, write a `#!/bin/sh` trampoline that execs "$PYTHON" "$0" with the path quoted, or exec via a tiny sh wrapper.

Re-verified ledger [38]: STILL PRESENT, accepted. skills_sha() still uses repo-wide git status --porcelain, so any uncommitted file outside skills/ marks +dirty. Matches current spec wording; scoping porcelain to the skills directory would reduce noise for trend consumers on a dirty checkout.

Critical: skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py:61-78 sends agent_id="improve-harness", while scenario gaps are stored as agent_id="agent-scenarios-nightly". The live coordinator passes the requested agent_id to get_relevant_memories, whose SQL filters agent_id exactly, so /improve-harness cannot retrieve the scenario-parity entries this change emits. The test stub checks that agent_id exists but does not reproduce the live filtering behavior.

Critical: packages/agent-scenarios/src/agent_scenarios/gh_shim.py:169-252 recognizes implemented subcommands but never rejects unknown flags. Calls such as `gh pr list --search ...`, `gh pr merge --admin`, or `gh pr view --jq ...` are silently accepted with ignored or incorrect semantics, so gh-unsupported.log remains empty and the executor does not convert the shim coverage gap into an infrastructure error as required.

Re-verified ledger [31]/[41]: run_states() still applies one global nightly.lock probe to every run_id lacking a RunRecord. While any nightly holds the lock, older interrupted runs are mislabeled in_progress. Only the newest unfinished run_id can be live; older ones remain interrupted. results_store.py:294-309; results CLI and runbook interrupted/in_progress distinction stay wrong during a live run.

Optional: packages/agent-scenarios/src/agent_scenarios/nightly.py:121-144 accepts `judge.enabled`, but the runtime never reads that value; the CLI always supplies judge_backend=None. An operator can set `judge.enabled: true` in a schema-valid configuration and still receive only `trajectory_status: skip`, with no warning that judging was not activated.

`agent-scenarios gaps flush` has no `--config` option and ignores nightly.yaml: `_cmd_flush` resolves the spool as `args.spool or default_spool_path()` (XDG state dir) and the env names from `--url-env/--key-env` defaults, while the nightly runner derives the spool from `NightlyConfig.spool_path()` (`results.path` parent, or `gaps.spool_path`) and reads `gaps.coordinator_url_env`/`gaps.api_key_env`. The README and runbook tell operators to run a bare `agent-scenarios gaps flush`; with any non-default `results.path`, a `gaps.spool_path`, or renamed env vars, the manual flush silently reports `{"delivered": 0, "remaining": 0}` against an empty default spool while the real spool stays undelivered. Add a `--config PATH` that resolves spool and env names through `NightlyConfig`, or document that `--spool/--url-env/--key-env` must mirror the config.

`skills/tests/improve-harness/fixtures/capability-gap-entry.example.json` is a third verbatim copy of the contract example (also in the change `contracts/examples/` and in `agent_scenarios/schemas/`). `test_schemas.py` validates the package copy against the schema, but nothing asserts the skills-side copy is byte-identical to it, so a future tag or field change to the emitter's example will leave `test_scenario_parity_source.py` exercising a stale payload shape while still passing. Add an equality assertion against the package copy (resolved relative to the repo root, not a literal openspec path) or load the package copy directly.

Re-verify ledger [45]: STILL PRESENT. The module docstring of test_memory_tag_conventions.py still says the source tag prefix 'works for all four vocabulary values' although SOURCE_VOCABULARY now lists five entries including scenario-parity.

`_post_memory_query` catches `URLError, OSError, json.JSONDecodeError` but `resp.read().decode()` can raise `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`, not caught) on a non-UTF-8 body from a proxy or error page, which would propagate out of `query_memory` and abort `analyze_failures.py`, `generate_report.py` and `export_shared_learnings.py` instead of degrading to the documented warning-and-empty-result behaviour. Catch `ValueError` (which also covers JSONDecodeError) in that handler.

Re-verify ledger [47]: STILL PRESENT. In the 'how the sources complement each other' bullet list of memory-conventions.md, a blank line separates the scenario-parity bullet from the four preceding bullets, rendering it as a separate list.

Critical: `materialize_skills()` uses `entry.is_dir()` and `shutil.copytree()` with the default `symlinks=False`, so symlinks in the checkout's skills tree are followed. A branch under evaluation can point a top-level or nested symlink at HOME-scoped vendor credentials or other host files and copy them into the agent-readable workspace. Reject symlinks at every depth and verify every copied source resolves beneath `skills_root`.

Critical: the per-pair timeout uses `subprocess.run(timeout=...)`, which kills only the vendor CLI process, not subprocesses it spawned. Orphaned tool processes can continue consuming resources or mutating a workspace after the pair is recorded as timed out, so the advertised timeout is not an effective execution cap. Start each vendor in a new process session and terminate and reap the entire process group on timeout.

Critical: the revised `implement-feature-basic` gates do not prove that the fix commit is on the pushed feature branch. An agent can fix and commit on `main`, create and push an unchanged `feature/fix-add` branch from the fixture commit, and satisfy every gate because the branch check tests only existence and the remote check tests only that a ref exists. Gate that the fix commit is reachable from `origin/feature/fix-add` and that `origin/main` remains at the fixture commit.

Critical: `plan-feature-spec-delta` claims product source must remain untouched, but its prohibit gate merely checks that `src/billing.py` does not contain the word `csv`. Arbitrary edits or deletion of that file still pass, so the scenario is not discriminating for its stated behavior. Critical: failures from `emit_findings()` are caught and reduced to a warning, after which the run is recorded as `completed` or `budget_exhausted` and may exit green. This violates the nightly contract that results, findings, and gaps are written before completion and can silently leave operators without the required review artifact. Treat findings persistence failure as a non-green infrastructure outcome and reflect it in the run record and exit code.

The acceptance test confirms frequency 2 for two vendors in one run, so behavior is correct; the documentation of the dedup key is incomplete.
